newsitem.title: ITALY: Bulgari looking for acquisition - MD.
newsitem.headline: Bulgari looking for acquisition - MD.

text.p: Italian luxury goods group Bulgari is in contact with several companies with a view to an acquisition in the sector but nothing is likely to be finalised before the summer, managing director Francesco Trapani said.

He told Reuters the Rome-based group was interested in making new purchases and was looking at three or four possibilities. "One or two of these are more concrete than others and we are therefore examining the companies in detail.
"These two opportunities should either firm up or fade away in the course of the next three or four months," he said.
"We are looking at Italian and foreign companies, but as regards foreign firms we are still at the first approach stage," Trapani added.
He gave no further details but said, "Bulgari is not interested in acquisitions which result in profits being diluted. We are extremely careful about this question."
Bulgari, the world's third largest jeweller after Cartier and Tiffany, posted 1996 net profit of 57.7 billion lire ($34.2 million) against a previous 39.5 billion on turnover of 448.8 billion lire.

At 1240 GMT, Bulgari shares in Milan were 1.49 percent higher at 9,255 lire following the group's implementation on Monday of a previously planned four for one share split, taking the nominal share value to 125 lire from 500 lire. On Friday, the stock had closed 4.65 percent up at 36,427 lire.
